blocks.text: Grouping DLP & Endpoint resources allows you to apply Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy rules to multiple resources at the same time. Additionally, you can use tags to build custom application lists for Endpoint Context. After you create a resource tag group, you add that group to the Endpoint DLP policy rules that you configure. For example, suppose that you work at a company with corporate headquarters in the United States, but you want to apply a country-specific set of endpoint policy rules to the network printers in your Canadian branch office. In that case, you can create a DLP resource group that includes all network printers in the branch office, and then you apply the policy rules to the resource group you created.

blocks.item: Resource groups are replaced by resource tags for Endpoint DLP. Any resource groups that you have already configured are automatically converted to resource tag groups. All policies that previously used resource groups are automatically updated to use the converted resource tag groups.
If your organization has licensed Endpoint Context but not Endpoint DLP, you do not have the option to create tags for network shares, network printers, or removable storage devices.

blocks.text: To add a DLP and endpoint resource tag:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint DLP Resources.
On the DLP & Endpoint Resources page:
Create a network share tag
On the Network Share Tags page (Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint DLP Resources > Network Share Tags):
Click Add Tag.
The Add Tag - Network Shares window appears.
In the Add Tag - Network Shares window:
Enter the following Basic information:
Name: The name of the network share tag
Description: (Optional) A description of the network share tag
Select the network shares you want to add to the tag, then click Add Tag.
See image.
The new tag appears in the list of network share tags on the Network Share Tags page.
See image.
Create a network printers tag
On the Printer Tags page (Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint DLP Resources > Printer Tags):
Click Add Tag.
The Add Tag - Printers window appears.
In the Add Tag - Printers window:
Enter the following Basic information:
Name: The name of the printer tag
Description: (Optional) A description of the printer tag
Select the network printers you want to add to the tag, then click Add Tag.
See image.
The new tag appears in the list of printer tags on the Printer Tags page.
See image.
Create a removable storage device tag
On the Removable Storage Device Tags (Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint DLP Resources > Removable Storage Device Tags) page:
Click Add Tag.
The Add Tag - Removable Storage Devices window appears.
In the Add Tag - Removable Storage Devices window:
Enter the following Basic information:
Name: The name of the storage device tag
Description: (Optional) A description of the storage device tag
Select the storage devices you want to add to the tag, then click Add Tag.
See image.
The new tag appears in the list of removable storage device tags on the Removable Storage Device Tags page.
See image.
Create an endpoint application tag
To access this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.

The Endpoint Application Tags tab contains both prebuilt lists of applications by category or theme from Zscaler, such as “Certificate Pinned” or “AI Browsers”, but can also contain custom application lists specific to your organization. You can click Edit on an existing customized prebuilt list.
On the Endpoint Application Tags page (Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint DLP Resources > Endpoint Application Tags):
Click Add Endpoint Application Tag.
The Add Endpoint Application Tag drawer opens.
In the Add Endpoint Application Tag drawer:
Enter the following basic information:
Name: The name of the application tag
Description: (Optional) A description of the application tag
In the Endpoint Applications drop-down menu, select applications to which you want to apply the tag, then click Apply.
See image.
Click Add.
The new tag appears in the list of application tags on the Endpoint Application Tags page.
See image.
Activate your changes.
